hint.text:
A comma’s placement in a sentence can completely change its meaning.

For example:
“Leila ate chocolate, ice cream and strawberries.”
“Leila ate chocolate ice cream and strawberries.”

By removing the comma, Leila goes from eating three different foods to just two.

instruction.text: Match the sentences to their meaning based on the placement of the commas.

atoms.a: Fred bought a pretty large ring.
atoms.b: The ring that Fred bought was quite big.

atoms.a: Fred bought a pretty, large ring.
atoms.b: The ring that Fred bought was beautiful and big.

instruction.text: Match the sentences to their meaning based on the placement of the commas.

atoms.a: Derek’s favourite things are eating his mouse and his friends.
atoms.b: Derek eats his mouse and his friends.

atoms.a: Derek’s favourite things are eating, his mouse and his friends.
atoms.b: Derek enjoys eating and spending time with his mouse and his friends.

instruction.text: Match the sentences to their meaning based on the placement of the commas.

atoms.a: Tabitha thought the nurse was very alert.
Tabitha, thought the nurse, was very alert.

instruction.text: Select the sentence that matches the description.

feedback.wrong: The sentence, “Hurry up and cook Dad.” suggests that the child would like to cook their father.

atoms.a: A child asking their father to cook soon.

instruction.text: Select the sentence that matches the description.

feedback.wrong: The sentence, “After leaving, Miles, Kaia and Lou went to the park.” suggests that three people went to the park.

atoms.a: Only two people went to the park.
b: ++After leaving Miles, Kaia and Lou went to the park.
After leaving, Miles, Kaia and Lou went to the park.

instruction.text: Select the sentence that matches the description.

wrong.text: The sentence, “Maya, believes Rhian, is an amazing cook.” suggests that Rhian thinks that Maya is a good cook.

atoms.a: Maya thinks that Rhian is a good cook.
b: Maya, believes Rhian, is an amazing cook.
++Maya believes Rhian is an amazing cook.
